subject: Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
query: why are there two dan sullivans on the alaska ballot
title: Why are there two Dan Sullivans on the Alaska ballot?
answer: Two Dan Sullivans are on Alaska's 2026 Senate ballot because a second man with the same name, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a retired teacher from Petersburg, filed to run against Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan. The state tried to disqualify him, but Alaska's courts ordered his name kept on the ballot.
body:
Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. is a retired teacher and former U.S. Forest Service employee. He filed as a Republican three days before the deadline, called himself a pragmatic centrist, and says he is no relation to the senator. Senator Sullivan called the bid a sham and dirty politics by Democrats. Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign and the state and national Democratic parties denied any link, though Alaska station KTUU found he had given small donations to Peltola's past campaigns, $100 in 2022 and $30 in 2024.

The Division of Elections ruled on June 16, 2026 that his filing was not made in good faith and removed him. An Anchorage Superior Court judge reversed that on June 26, and the Alaska Supreme Court agreed on July 2. In the August top-four primary he won about 2.5%, enough to reach the November ballot. To limit confusion, the ballot lists him as "Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr." with no party, and marks Dan S. Sullivan as the incumbent.

He drew roughly 3,600 votes, about 1.7%, in the first count of the Nov. 3 general election, a race in which Peltola led the senator by only about 600 votes. Under ranked-choice rules he will be eliminated early, and his ballots will move to his voters' second choices in the count scheduled for Nov. 18.
in_the_news: The Alaska Senate race between Mary Peltola and Senator Dan Sullivan is separated by a few hundred votes, and the second Sullivan's ballots could matter when ranked choices are counted on Nov. 18, 2026.

faq.q: Is Daniel J. Sullivan related to Senator Dan Sullivan?
faq.a: No. He says he has no relation to the senator; they simply share a name.

faq.q: How many votes did the other Dan Sullivan get?
faq.a: About 3,600 votes, roughly 1.7%, in early general election results, and about 2.5% in the August primary.

faq.q: What happens to votes for Daniel J. Sullivan?
faq.a: In the ranked-choice count, he is likely to be eliminated early, and each of his ballots moves to that voter's next-ranked candidate, if they ranked one.
